description: REQ-204's own stated purpose is to make REQ-203's 'no steering text that tells the model WHICH of the remaining options to prefer' principle actually true of runtime/loop/prompt.mjs -- the spec says verbatim: 'Leaving both mechanisms in place simultaneously after this increment ships would mean REQ-203's "no steering text" principle is false of the codebase in the very increment that establishes it.' But REQ-204's Acceptance Criteria scope the removal to only THREE named things: the '## ★COLONY BOOTSTRAP PRIORITY★' block's imperative language, the phrase 'Prefer this over re-yielding surplus', and the phrase 'it is almost never "yield again"'. REQ-204's own Edge Cases section makes this scoping explicit and exclusive: 'REQ-204 targets only the imperative/ranking language named above.' I re-read the ACTUAL current runtime/loop/prompt.mjs end-to-end (lines 45-132, buildSystemPrompt). The '## Your earn tools' section (lines 69-88), which is NOT the '★COLONY BOOTSTRAP PRIORITY★' block and is never named by REQ-204, contains its own independent ranking statement in the exact same bullet/paragraph as the already-flagged 'Prefer this over re-yielding surplus' phrase: 'economy/gig : ★THE LABOR MARKET — the colony economy★ When you have USDC SURPLUS above your reserve, THE HIGHEST-LEVERAGE MOVE IS TO POST a real bounded sub-task...' (line 71). 'The highest-leverage move is X' is a textbook instance of the exact thing REQ-203 prohibits in its own words ('any scoring/ranking of the remaining options, or any steering text that tells the model WHICH of the remaining options to prefer') -- it explicitly ranks posting a gig above the other listed tools (hl_trade, x402_sell, token_launch, yield) whenever there is surplus. This phrase sits five lines before, in the same paragraph as, the 'Prefer this over re-yielding surplus' phrase that REQ-204 DOES name -- proving the spec's authors were already reading this exact paragraph closely enough to quote one ranking phrase from it, yet stopped short of the other ranking phrase one sentence earlier. Because REQ-204's Acceptance Criteria are keyed to three specific quoted strings (and PROP-204a's Tool/Method column literally says 'grep/read runtime/loop/prompt.mjs for the specific quoted phrases above'), a Phase 3 implementation that removes exactly and only those three things would fully satisfy REQ-204's own acceptance criteria and PROP-204a, while 'the highest-leverage move is to POST' -- an equally real, equally pre-existing violation of REQ-203's own stated principle -- remains untouched in the shipped file. This creates an internal contradiction between two proof obligations describing the SAME code state: PROP-204a would report PASS (all three named phrases gone) while PROP-203b ('no pre-existing steering block of equivalent strength remains in the file's binding sections') would have to report FAIL for the identical file -- the exact kind of non-binary, reviewer-dependent outcome VCSDD's proof-obligation design is meant to prevent. REQ-204 is the specific mechanism this increment relies on to close REQ-203's gap; its enumerated target list is measurably incomplete relative to the very principle it exists to satisfy.
